beats.intro: Chapter eight, lesson six. The active site and how enzymes catalyse. [[lock]]A key fits one lock, and ignores all the others. A glove fits one hand, and hugs it. [[cells]]Inside a cell, enzymes work in much the same way. [[strip]]Here is our pathway strip again, with enzyme one lit. [[zoom]]Today we zoom in on the one small region of the enzyme where the chemistry happens.
beats.spec: [[sub]]The reactant that an enzyme acts on is called its substrate. [[site]]The substrate binds to a region of the enzyme called the active site. It is a small pocket, a groove or a notch on the surface, formed by just a few of the enzyme's amino acids. [[complex]]While the substrate sits in the active site, the pair is called the enzyme-substrate complex. [[shape]]Enzymes are specific. The shape and chemistry of the pocket match one substrate, or a few close relatives. A molecule with the wrong shape cannot bind, so the enzyme ignores it. [[sucr]]Sucrase, from last lesson, splits sucrose, but leaves other sugars alone. That is why a cell needs a different enzyme for every step of a pathway.
beats.fit: [[open]]At first, the pocket is not a perfect mould. [[close]]When the substrate enters, the active site changes shape a little and closes in around it. This is called induced fit. It brings the chemical groups of the active site into positions where they can catalyse the reaction. [[glove]]Think of a hand sliding into a glove. The glove is loose, and then it hugs. [[back]]Notice what this means. The enzyme flexes, but it is not used up. When the products leave, it springs back to its first shape, ready for the next substrate.
beats.q1: Quick check. What does induced fit mean?
beats.ways: [[ea]]Remember the activation energy barrier from last lesson, the hump a reaction must climb. The active site can lower that hump in four ways. [[orient]]First, it orients the substrates correctly, so they meet in just the right position. [[strain]]Second, it strains the substrate's bonds, stretching them so they break more easily. [[micro]]Third, it provides a favourable microenvironment. For example, the pocket can be more acidic than the cell around it. [[cov]]Fourth, it can bond covalently to the substrate for a moment, and then let go. [[lower]]Whichever way it works, the hump gets lower, and the reaction speeds up. But the energy change, delta G, stays exactly the same.
beats.cycle: Now the whole catalytic cycle, in six steps. [[c1]]One. Two substrates enter the active site. [[c2]]Two. They are held there by weak interactions, such as hydrogen bonds and ionic bonds. That makes the enzyme-substrate complex. [[c3]]Three. The active site lowers the activation energy, and speeds up the reaction. [[c4]]Four. The substrates are converted to products. [[c5]]Five. The products are released. [[c6]]Six. The active site is empty again, and available for two new substrate molecules. [[loop]]Then the same enzyme goes round again, and again, without being used up.
beats.q2: Quick check. Put four steps of the cycle in order.
beats.sat: [[few]]Now a worked example. Say a cell has a fixed number of enzyme molecules, like a row of checkout counters. With only a little substrate, most active sites sit empty, and the reaction is slow. [[more]]Add more substrate, and the rate climbs, because more active sites are busy. [[full]]But there are only so many active sites. Soon every one is occupied. This is called saturation. Adding even more substrate cannot speed things up, because the enzymes are already working as fast as they can. It is like a shop at rush hour: every counter is busy, and the queue just grows. [[add]]The only way to go faster is to have more enzyme.
beats.wrap: [[w1]]To sum up. The substrate binds to the active site, forming the enzyme-substrate complex. [[w2]]The shapes match, so enzymes are specific, and induced fit closes the pocket around the substrate. [[w3]]The active site lowers the activation energy by orienting the substrates, straining their bonds, providing a favourable microenvironment, or bonding to them covalently. [[w4]]The cycle repeats, and the rate levels off at saturation. [[end]]Now try the practice.
